conclusion: Keep the single radius-two rule and all three controls. Freeze the distinctions below between what the rooted record decides, what a funded cut actually does and what a marked pair eventually inherits. No new outcomes were executed or examined for this advice.

changes.advice: The induced record is well-defined up to simultaneous renaming and exchange of the root holders. Prove the cutoff in the graph with e removed: distance to the nearer endpoint is unchanged by deleting e. The displayed set is the union of the two radius-two balls there. They can join through a common holder or one internal meeting precisely when an alternate route has at most five meetings. Include detours of exactly five and six; unequal chain lengths cover the even case omitted by equal arms. Degrees on a boundary holder can change when an edited chain end lies inside the displayed record. For a no-go for arbitrary fixed radius r, put both edited holders strictly beyond r and explicitly match every supplied count and parallel incidence. Radius bounds reach, while the record size can grow with arity.

For one donor at each side of e, a shared ordinary group would supply a route of at most two meetings between donors. Any other added group gives one of at most three using its own key and live-to-spent incidences, so it avoids e. Adding the terminal meetings would give an alternative to e of at most five. Use this to test uniqueness of the focal group's origin even on a long circuit. Overlap among donors of distinct groups still costs one per group. On identical held inputs record ordinary charges, extra charges, current supply, unary remainder, global funding, the complete paid group and its fresh grant. Suppressing one permission there isolates its effect. Separate histories under two policies can already differ in their previous grants.

At the first provisional cut an originally separating name can lose separation only if some new child has donors in both original parts. Every eligible group has pairwise original holder separation at most three. A shortest old route between opposite donors passes through the name; using their child gives its endpoints a bypass of at most four meetings. This is a route to age-one equality on trees, and on a larger sufficient class where each relevant originally nonseparating name already has a bypass of length at most five. Check actual age-zero groups, age-one provisional groups and equality of age-zero prices before invoking the coeval disjointness induction. For seven knots use the short original circuits and parallel names; for 21 check both original spent pairs and original live-to-live meetings. Forecast with one placeholder is sound only because eligibility uses positive loose count, independently of its size; check the sole zero-fresh parity close.

changes.topic: Paid arrival, price matching and finite samples
changes.advice: In the open/closed arm declare the same two specific live terminal donors, one on each side, as the ancestry query. The spent key identifies eligibility and supplies no true parent. Show both arms fund, then test one-step common descent and any later first arrival using all actual parents; a capped nonmeeting is censored. For the private-name edit match existing birth slots on their true parents and inherited names, including repeated unaries. Keep the focal group's own grant, all grants of other children of A, and the earliest subsequently unmatched birth as separate outputs. The prior distant-edit theorem already refutes exact local emulation of global separation; an added contribution requires the paid output on the matched preparations or a history-equality proof. Freeze the remote-length distribution, all RNG seeds, pairing across laws and rules, and one-vote-per-start denominator before sampling.
